question.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 1 & -3 & 7\end{aligned}]
$$

If the matrix $A$ above is diagonalizable, find a corresponding diagonal matrix $D.$
question.worked_solution:
Since the matrix $A$ is triangular, its eigenvalues are the entries of the main diagonal. Therefore, the eigenvalues are ${\lambda }_{1}=7$ (simple root) and ${\lambda }_{2}=4$ (double root).

Let's now find the dimension of the eigenspace corresponding to each eigenvalue.

- First, we consider the simple root ${\lambda }_{1}=7.$ Since the root is simple, the dimension of the eigenspace ${V}_{7}$ corresponding to ${\lambda }_{1}=7$ is

$$
\text{dim}({V}_{7})=1.
$$

- Next, we consider the double root ${\lambda }_{2}=4.$ Let's find the dimension of the eigenspace ${V}_{4}$ corresponding to this eigenvalue. To do this, we row-reduce the matrix $A-4I:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A-4I & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 1 & -3 & 7\end{aligned}]-4[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & -3 & 3\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}↔{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). This implies that we will have $3-1=2$ linearly independent eigenvectors corresponding to ${\lambda }_{2}=4.$ So, 

$$
\text{dim}({V}_{4})=2.
$$

Therefore, $A$ is diagonalizable, since

$$
\text{dim}({V}_{7})+\text{dim}({V}_{4})=1+2=3.\,✓
$$

Finally, the corresponding diagonal matrix is 

$$
D=[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 7\end{aligned}].
$$
